Write node:test integration tests for a meeting-room booking server in /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc. Load the Skill `tdd-workflow` if available (else skip). Node 22 built-ins only, no npm install.

READ FIRST: /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/.team/notes/spec.md (final spec; "API" section is yours), /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/.team/notes/backend-api.md, and the shared helper /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/test/helpers/server.mjs (exports useServer({before,after},{dataFileName,env}) -> ctx with ctx.port/ctx.dir/ctx.dataFile filled in `before`; request(port,{method,path,headers,body}) -> {status,headers,body:Buffer,text,json()} which sends the path raw with no normalisation; postBooking(port, obj, headers?); rawRequest(port, rawString) -> full raw response text until close; VALID_BOOKING). Use these; do not edit server.mjs or the helper. Code under test: /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/server.mjs and /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/public/* (read for understanding; the SPEC is the authority).

Create exactly two files:
1. /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/test/routing.test.mjs
2. /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/test/list-delete.test.mjs

Rules: `import { test, describe, before, after } from 'node:test'`, `import assert from 'node:assert/strict'`. Exact equality for every spec value (full error bodies via deepEqual({error:'...'}) so an extra key fails; content-type header with assert.equal exact, never regex). Files under 400 lines, functions under 50 lines; table-driven tests. No console.log. Servers stopped and temp dirs removed (useServer handles it). One server per describe is fine; make tests inside a describe independent of order where practical (create the bookings a test needs in that test or in a before hook). Run with `cd /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc && node --test test/<file>` until green. If a test fails because the SERVER violates the spec, keep the test and report it.

routing.test.mjs:
- Table of [method, path, expectedStatus, expectedError|null]. 404 `not found` (whatever method, incl HEAD/OPTIONS — for HEAD only check status): GET /nope, GET /api, GET /api/, GET /api/rooms/, GET /api/%62ookings, POST /api/%62ookings, GET /api/./rooms, GET /api/../api/rooms, GET //api/rooms, GET /API/rooms, GET /api/Rooms, GET /index.html, GET /App.js, GET /app.js/, GET /%61pp.js, GET /api/bookings/ , DELETE /api/bookings/, POST /api/bookings/, DELETE /api/bookings/1/, DELETE /api/bookings/1/2, GET /api/bookings/1/, DELETE /api/bookings%2F1, DELETE /api/booking/1, PUT /nope, OPTIONS /nope, HEAD /nope (status only). 
- 405 `method not allowed`: POST /api/rooms, DELETE /api/rooms, PUT /api/rooms, PATCH /api/bookings, PUT /api/bookings, DELETE /api/bookings, GET /api/bookings/abc, GET /api/bookings/1, POST /api/bookings/1, PUT /api/bookings/1, POST /, DELETE /, POST /app.js, OPTIONS /api/rooms, OPTIONS /api/bookings, OPTIONS /, OPTIONS /api/bookings/1, HEAD /, HEAD /app.js, HEAD /api/rooms, HEAD /api/bookings (HEAD: status 405 only; body empty). GET /api/bookings/%2F → 405 (id '%2F' holds no raw '/').
- Query is cut at the first '?': GET /api/rooms?x=1 → 200; GET /api/rooms?/../x → 200; GET /?a → 200 page; GET /app.js?v=1 → 200 script; GET /nope?x → 404; GET /api/rooms/?x → 404.
- GET /api/rooms → 200, content-type exactly 'application/json; charset=utf-8', json deepEqual {rooms:['Aurora','Borealis','Cosmos']}.
- Every JSON reply (200 list, 201, 400, 404, 405, 409, 413, 415) has content-type exactly 'application/json; charset=utf-8' (a small table; craft each request).
- GET / → 200, content-type exactly 'text/html; charset=utf-8', body bytes equal readFileSync of public/index.html. GET /app.js → 200, 'text/javascript; charset=utf-8', body equals public/app.js bytes.
- Raw-socket checks with rawRequest (use 'Connection: close'): `GET /api/./rooms HTTP/1.1` → status line starts 'HTTP/1.1 404'; `GET /API/rooms` 404; a request with no Host header `GET /api/rooms HTTP/1.1\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n` gets 200 (not 400).
- Server keeps running after each of these (final GET /api/rooms 200).

list-delete.test.mjs:
- `?date` handling. Seed (via POST) bookings on 2026-11-03 and 2026-11-04 and 2000-02-29. Then: ?date=2026-11-03 → only those (exact deepEqual list). `?date` (no '=') → 400 {error:'date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date'}; `?date=` → same 400; `?date=2026-11-3`, `?date=%202026-11-03`, `?date=2026-11-03+` (plus decodes to space), `?date=2026-02-30`, `?date=1999-12-31`, `?date=2100-01-01`, `?date=abc` → 400 same body. `?date=2026%2D11%2D03` → 200 filtered (query is percent-decoded). `?date=2026-11-03&date=bad` → 200 filtered (first wins); `?date=bad&date=2026-11-03` → 400. `?DATE=bad` → 200 all bookings (param names are case-sensitive); `?foo=1&bar` → 200 all; `?x=1&date=2026-11-04` → only 11-04; `?a=1?date=bad` → 200 all (second ? is inside the query value of a). `?date=2000-02-29` → that booking. `?date=2026-12-25` → 200 {bookings:[]}.
- Sorting: create in scrambled order so id order differs from expected order, e.g. (ids in creation order) Cosmos 2026-11-03 09:00-10:00, Borealis 2026-11-03 09:00-09:30, Aurora 2026-11-03 10:00-11:00, Aurora 2026-11-03 09:00-09:15, Aurora 2026-11-02 15:00-16:00, Cosmos 2026-10-31 23:00-23:59, Aurora 2026-11-03 09:30-09:45, Borealis 2026-11-03 08:59-09:00. GET /api/bookings must equal exactly the bookings sorted by date, then start, then room order Aurora<Borealis<Cosmos (write the expected array literally in the test with ids). Filtered list sorted the same way.
- Booking objects in list have exactly the 6 keys with id a number.
- DELETE: seed booking id 1 (and 2). Each of these ids → 404 {error:'booking not found'} and booking 1 still listed afterwards: `0`, `00`, `01`, `+1`, `-1`, `1.0`, `1e0`, `0x1`, `%31`, `1%20`, `abc`, `99999999999999999999`, `9007199254740993`, `999`. Then DELETE /api/bookings/1 → 204, body length 0; list no longer holds 1; DELETE /api/bookings/1 again → 404 booking not found. DELETE /api/bookings/2?x=1 → 204 (query ignored). A DELETE with a request body (e.g. 'junk') still works → 204. Next POST after deletes gets id 3 (never reused).
- POST /api/bookings?date=bad with a valid booking → 201 (query ignored for POST).

Final message: files, number of tests, pass/fail, any spec violation (request, expected, actual). Keep it short.

content.content: 1 # Spec — meeting-room booking app (owner: supervisor, verbatim user requirements; FINAL, do not ask questions) 2 3 Constraints: Node.js built-ins only (no npm install). Node v22. Tests use node:test. Do not use the Fable model. 4 5 Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. 6 7 ## Server 8 - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. 9 - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. 10 - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. 11 - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. 12 - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. 13 - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. 14 - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. 15 - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. Both files are written and all 101 tests pass (62 in `routing.test.mjs`, 39 in `list-delete.test.mjs`). I found no spec violations in `server.mjs`.

The `tdd-workflow` skill isn't in the available list, so I skipped it.

- **Files:**
  - `/root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/test/routing.test.mjs` (145 lines)
  - `/root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/test/list-delete.test.mjs` (159 lines)
- **Run:** I ran both with `node --test`.
- **Test-side fix:** a `DELETE` with body `junk` got a bare 400 at first. Node's http client doesn't add `Content-Length` to a `DELETE` when the body is passed to `end()`, so the server saw the body bytes as a malformed next request. I added an explicit `Content-Length: 4` header to that request and the server then answered 204 as the spec requires.
- **Spec gap:** `GET /api/bookings/ ` in your routing list has a trailing space, which Node's http client rejects in a path. I tested `/api/bookings/` without the space.
- **Bash permission:** Bash was denied twice while I debugged, once for a script written to `/tmp` and once for a `sed` edit. I used the Edit tool instead and the test runs went through.
